journal.oldrepublic.chapter: Chapter One: Echoes in the Stone
journal.oldrepublic.empty: The pages are blank. Whatever this book is for, it has not begun yet.
journal.oldrepublic.progress.calling: The note is clear while I hold the journal. Follow the shimmer.
journal.oldrepublic.progress.calling_fai: The note is faint here. Whatever calls is far away; I should travel and listen again.
quest.oldrepublic.objective.stirring: Something is stirring, but not yet.
quest.oldrepublic.objective.focus: Calm the disturbance. Crouch and stay perfectly still with this journal in hand until the noise settles.
quest.oldrepublic.objective.practice: Learn what the Force can do. Push back hostile creatures with it (Use Force Power).
quest.oldrepublic.objective.calling: Follow the pull. Hold this journal, watch for the shimmer and listen for the note; it is loudest when I face it.
quest.oldrepublic.objective.trial: Find what sings at the heart of the cave and face the trial waiting there.
quest.oldrepublic.objective.construction: Give the crystal a body: gather an emitter, a grip and a pommel, and build my lightsaber at a workbench.
quest.oldrepublic.objective.complete: The first chapter is closed. Somewhere out there is a teacher.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_dream.body:
I am writing this down because I do not trust myself to remember it right.

Last night I dreamt of a dark place under the ground, full of voices. Not words. Something older than words, and every one of them was turned toward me.

When I woke, everything around me had been thrown away from me. Leaves stripped from the branches, loose things scattered, as if I had shouted with my whole body. I did not move. I am sure I did not move.

My hands still feel as if they are humming. If this happens again near anyone, someone could get hurt. I need to be still. I need to find out what this is.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.stillness.body:
I knelt, I breathed, and I waited for the humming to stop. It did not stop. It settled, like dust after a storm, and underneath it there was something vast and quiet that had always been there.

When I stood and opened my hand, the air in front of me moved. Not wind. It moved because I asked it to.

Spacers at the trading posts talk about the Jedi in the same breath as ghosts; nobody out here has seen one in years. Whatever I am, I had better learn what this can do before it decides for me. The things that hunt at night will teach me quickly enough.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_pull.title: The Pull
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_pull.body:
Again and again now I have thrown back something that meant to kill me, and every time it is easier to find the still place first.

Something else has begun. A thin, clear note at the back of my skull, like a glass struck once and never quite silent. It is faint in the open and stronger when I turn a certain way. When I hold this journal and listen, I can almost see it: a shimmer in the air, drifting off toward the horizon.

I do not know what is calling. I know it is calling me.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.voices_in_the_:
Found it. The note led me to a cave mouth, and I was not the first to find it.

There is a camp at the entrance: prefab shelters, cutting lasers, crates of broken crystal packed in foam. Whoever they are, they are armed, and they are carving the cave open one shard at a time. The crystals they dropped are dead. I picked one up and felt nothing at all.

Deeper in, the singing is louder than ever. Whatever calls me is still down there, and they have not reached it yet.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.cutters.title: Cutters
journal.oldrepublic.entry.cutters.body:
One of the cutters came at me with a blaster and did not stop until I stopped him. Afterwards I went through his kit: a cheap rifle, a cutting charge, a datapad of payment chits under three different names, and a fine little emitter assembly he must have pried out of something far older than he was.

He could not hear the crystals. I am sure of that now. To him they were credits in the rock.
A bolt came straight for my chest and I knew where it would be before it got there. I moved, and it went back the way it came.

I have no idea how. I am writing it down so that tomorrow I believe it happened.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.what_waits_bel:
At the heart of the cave there is a chamber sealed in stone that opened when I touched it. I knelt at the stone in its centre, the way I do when I meditate, and something rose out of the dark to meet me.

It had my shape. It knew every move before I made it, because they were my moves.

I will go back. Next time I will not fight it the way it expects.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.reflection.bod:
I went back down and knelt again, and when it rose I did not look away.

It fought the way I fight when I am afraid, and every time I answered fear with fear it grew stronger. When I stopped trying to destroy it and simply saw it for what it was, it came apart like smoke in the wind.

Where it stood, the stone is warm, and the singing has narrowed to a single clear note.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_crystal.bo:
It grew on the stone while I watched, and when I picked it up it was warm and it was mine. I cannot put it any better than that. The cutters' crystals were dead in my hand. This one is awake.

The old stories say a crystal is the heart of a lightsaber, and a heart needs a body. I will need an emitter to shape the blade (the cutters carry them, salvaged from who knows where), a grip and a pommel. The cave has more chambers than their camp has mapped; something may be hidden there. And I will need a proper bench to put it all together.

Nobody has taught me how to do this. I am going to do it anyway, carefully.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.a_blade_of_my_:
It works.

The blade came up with a sound I felt in my teeth, and its light is the colour of the note I followed for so many days. It is rough. My hands made it, and they still have a great deal to learn.

Out here there is no Order and no Master, only rumours of ruins and the Jedi gone home to Tython. But I have a blade now, and a reason to go looking. The first chapter of this book is full. The next one begins with a teacher, if I can find one.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.the_force.body:
Every tradition I have heard of agrees on one thing: the Force is an energy that binds living things together, and a few beings feel it more clearly than others. The Jedi call it a light to be served with calm. Others call it a power to be taken.

What I know for certain is smaller. It answers stillness. It answers fear too, but not well.

Midi-chlorian Resonance: a measure of how strongly I am attuned. It grows only through great moments, never through repetition.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.cold_peace.bod:
Some years ago the Sith Empire came out of the dark and sacked Coruscant, and the treaty signed in its ashes ended the open war but not the hatred. The Republic rebuilds and watches its borders. The Jedi have left Coruscant for their ancient home on Tython. The Empire waits.

Out here, past the charted lanes, the peace means only that nobody is coming to help. Mercenaries, smugglers and scavengers fill the space the armies left behind.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.kyber.title: Kyber Crystals
journal.oldrepublic.codex.kyber.body:
Kyber crystals grow in a few hidden places, usually deep underground, and are said to be bound up with the Force itself. Spacers swear they sing to those who can hear. The Jedi make them the heart of their lightsabers, and it is said that a crystal chooses its bearer rather than the other way round.

To anyone else, a kyber crystal is a very valuable rock.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.poachers.title: Crystal Poachers
journal.oldrepublic.codex.poachers.body:
Crews of mercenaries and prospectors who strip crystal caves for buyers in the Core and beyond. They carry heavy blaster rifles, cutting tools, and salvaged lightsaber parts to sell on.

They keep their distance and fire in short bursts. Before each shot the muzzle glows and the rifle whines: that is the moment to move, or to be ready.

They cannot hear the crystals. They only hear the price.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.the_trial.body:
Some caves guard their deepest chamber with a seal that opens only for one who has begun to touch the Force. Within, a meditation stone waits. Whoever kneels there is met by an echo of themselves, shaped from their own habits and fears.

The echo cannot be outrun. It can be understood. Those who fail may return; the cave is patient, and nothing is lost but pride.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.lightsaber.bod:
A blade of plasma focused through a kyber crystal and shaped by an emitter, held in a hilt the builder makes by hand. The emitter changes the blade's reach and speed, the grip how long a guard can be held, the pommel the weight behind each cut. The colour comes from the crystal and means only what the bearer decides.

It is assembled at a workbench from a crystal, an emitter, a grip and a pommel.
dream.oldrepublic.line1: ...you have been asleep for so long...
dream.oldrepublic.line2: ...the stone remembers. The stone is singing...
hud.oldrepublic.level_up.title: Your attunement deepens
hud.oldrepublic.resonance_up.title: Midi-chlorian Resonance grows
message.oldrepublic.meditation_rested: Your mind is already settled today. Meditate again tomorrow.
message.oldrepublic.chapter_complete: Chapter One complete: Echoes in the Stone. (+%s skill points)
command.oldrepublic.journal.given: A Wanderer's Journal has been placed in your pack.
command.oldrepublic.journal.owned: You already carry a Wanderer's Journal.

dialogue.oldrepublic.crossing_jedi.greet: So the stone was not singing to itself. I am Ilyra Saelen, a Watchwoman of the Jedi Order; this stretch of the frontier is mine to keep. You have been touched by the Force, %s, and you found a crystal on your own. That is rare. It is also dangerous, alone.
dialogue.oldrepublic.crossing_jedi.more: The Order does not take what it finds. It teaches. I would show you how to reach without grasping, how to hold a blade without wanting to use it, and how to stand between the weak and those who would prey on them. It is slow. It is worth it.
dialogue.oldrepublic.crossing_jedi.treat: The Treaty of Coruscant ended the open war. It did not end the Empire. He and I may not raise blades against each other on neutral ground, and neither of us will be the one to break the peace in front of you. So we wait, and you choose.
dialogue.oldrepublic.crossing_jedi.other: He is not lying to you, which is what makes him dangerous. The Empire will give you strength quickly. It will ask you to pay for it in pieces of yourself, and it will never tell you the price in advance.
dialogue.oldrepublic.crossing_jedi.creed: Then tell me something first. An enemy lies beaten at your feet and begs. What do you do?
Hm. Answers are easy here. We will see what you do when it is real.
dialogue.oldrepublic.crossing_jedi.confi: Once you walk this road there is no simple way back. Follow the Jedi?
dialogue.oldrepublic.crossing_jedi.decli: You may walk your own way. The Force will not abandon you for it, but it will not make it easy either. Is that your answer?
dialogue.oldrepublic.crossing_jedi.opt.c: Let them live. They are no threat now.
Finish it. They would do the same to me.
dialogue.oldrepublic.crossing_sith.greet: Overseer Teyvar Sorn, of the Sith Empire. I came a long way for you, %s, and I do not say that to flatter. You pulled a crystal out of a cave full of armed men and walked out with it. The Empire has a place for people who take what is theirs.
dialogue.oldrepublic.crossing_sith.more: The Empire rewards strength, and only strength. No councils, no patience for its own sake. I will teach you to reach out and take, to strike first and hard, and to make sure nobody who wronged you does it twice.
dialogue.oldrepublic.crossing_sith.treat: A treaty is a pause, not a peace. If I cut her down on this ridge, the Republic would scream and my masters would have my head for the timing. So we stand here and smile. Enjoy it. It will not last.
dialogue.oldrepublic.crossing_sith.other: She will teach you to apologise for what you are. Mercy, restraint, patience. Fine words from people who lost a war and their capital with it.
dialogue.oldrepublic.crossing_sith.creed: Before you decide, an easy question. An enemy lies beaten at your feet and begs. What do you do?
Words. I will watch your hands, not your mouth.
dialogue.oldrepublic.crossing_sith.confi: Once you walk this road there is no simple way back. Follow the Sith?
dialogue.oldrepublic.crossing_sith.decli: Alone, then. The frontier eats people who think like that. Is that your answer?
dialogue.oldrepublic.crossing_sith.opt.c: Let them live. They are no threat now.
Finish it. They would do the same to me.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.idle: The frontier is quiet today. Quiet is not the same as safe.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.lesson_: Your first lesson is the oldest one, %s. Before you push the world away, learn to draw it to you. Reach for a thing with the Force and bring it near. Gently.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.why_pul: A push ends a conversation. A pull starts one. You can disarm a man, catch a child who slips, gather what was scattered. It is the most useful thing I know.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.lesson_: Pull five things to you: dropped tools and stones, or creatures that mean harm. Feel how little force it takes.
Now the blade. Form Three, Soresu: you do not win by striking, you win by not being struck. I will attack slowly and plainly. Turn three of my blows aside.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.questio: A question while we rest. A man steals bread from a homestead to feed his children. What is owed?
Remember that answer the next time someone steals from you.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.reckoni: Smoke on the ridge. The cutters you scattered at the cave have found a new captain, and they have taken settlers from a homestead. Go. Bring those people home.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.poacher: When you find them, and you will, what will you do with the poachers?
Then go and do it, and come back and tell me how it felt.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.debrief: You are back. Sit with me and tell me what happened on the ridge. All of it.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.trial: The Trial of the Blade waits when you are ready. You will duel me in earnest. I will not go easy, and I will stop the moment you have shown me enough.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.complet: Padawan %s. Sit with me a while; there is always more to learn.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.atone: Something heavy sits on you. Meditate beside me, here, today, and let it go. We will do this as often as it takes.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.unburde: Sometimes we carry the wrong lessons. I can help you set them all down and choose again. Are you sure?
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.session: Kneel beside me and meditate, within a few steps of me. I will guide you through it.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.opt.que: Food, and help. He should not have had to steal.
His hand. A thief is a thief.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.opt.poa: Stop them, and spare whoever yields.
Make sure they never come back.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.opt.tri: I am ready for the trial.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_jedi.opt.unb: I want to unlearn what I have learned.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_sith.idle: Do not waste my time. Train.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_sith.lesson_: First lesson, %s. The Force is not a gift; it is a hand. Reach out and drag your enemy to you, and kill them before they understand what happened.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_sith.why_pul: Because an enemy at a distance chooses the fight. An enemy at your feet does not.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_sith.lesson_: Pull three hostile creatures to you and kill each before it can recover. Quickly. Slow is the same as failed.
Brenn will teach you the rest. Form Four, Ataru: speed, weight, no pause. He hides behind his guard; break it. Land three heavy blows or lunges on him.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_sith.questio: A question. A man steals bread from you to feed his children. What is owed?
We will see whether you mean it.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_sith.reckoni: The scavengers from your cave have a new captain, and they raided a homestead. Take back what was stolen. Leave no witnesses.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_sith.poacher: And when they beg, as they will?
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_sith.trial: The Trial of Ascension. You and Brenn, in earnest. One of you rises today. I will stop it before you die, which is more mercy than the Empire usually shows.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_sith.complet: Apprentice %s. The Empire is watching you now. Do not disappoint it.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_sith.atone: You flinch. Kneel here, near me, and let the anger in instead of hiding from it. Once a day, until you stop flinching.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_sith.unburde: You would throw away everything you have learned and start again? Fine. Are you certain?
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_sith.session: Brenn is waiting, or the drill is. Spar.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_sith.opt.que: Everything he has. Thieves learn from losing.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_sith.opt.poa: If they yield, I'll let them go.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_sith.opt.tri: I am ready for the trial.
dialogue.oldrepublic.mentor_sith.opt.unb: I want to unlearn what I have learned.
dialogue.oldrepublic.brenn.decide: Go on, then. Finish it. Or don't. I'd want to know which kind of Apprentice you are.
dialogue.oldrepublic.brenn.spare_confirm: Spare him? Sorn will call it weakness. Spare Brenn?
dialogue.oldrepublic.brenn.kill_confirm: Kill him? There is no taking that back. Kill Brenn?
dialogue.oldrepublic.brenn.early: So you are the one Sorn dragged in from the frontier. Don't get comfortable.
dialogue.oldrepublic.brenn.who: Brenn Ostrak. I have been his acolyte for two years. You have been his for two days. Do the arithmetic.
dialogue.oldrepublic.brenn.default: Not now. When the Overseer says spar, we spar.
dialogue.oldrepublic.independent.name: The Two Voices
dialogue.oldrepublic.independent.voices: You still yourself and reach out, and two voices answer from far off: one warm, one cold. Either would still come, if you called. Only once.
dialogue.oldrepublic.independent.confirm: The warm voice. The Watchwoman will come for you, and the road will be hers. Call to her?
The cold voice. The Overseer will come for you, and the road will be his. Call to him?
dialogue.oldrepublic.independent.summon: You reach for your teacher across the distance. They would come to you, and make camp near here.
message.oldrepublic.story.path_forced: Your path was set to %s by an operator; Chapter Two follows it.
message.oldrepublic.story.not_yours.jedi: She is waiting for someone else.
message.oldrepublic.story.not_yours.sith: He is waiting for someone else.
message.oldrepublic.story.not_yours.bren: He is not here for you.
message.oldrepublic.story.arrived: Two figures wait here, blades lit, facing each other.
message.oldrepublic.story.blocked.jedi_r: The Watchwoman will not take you as you are now.
message.oldrepublic.story.blocked.sith_r: The Overseer will not take you as you are now.
message.oldrepublic.story.blocked.reputa: Their order distrusts you too much.
message.oldrepublic.story.blocked.rep_je: Requires Trusted standing with the Jedi Order.
message.oldrepublic.story.blocked.rep_si: Requires Trusted standing with the Sith Empire.
message.oldrepublic.story.spar_unavailab: There is no one here to spar with.
message.oldrepublic.story.summoned: %s has heard you and is on the way.
message.oldrepublic.story.smoke_seen: Smoke rises from a ridge somewhere nearby. Hold the journal to feel which way.
message.oldrepublic.story.report_back: It is done. %s will want to hear about it.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.name: Master Ilyra Saelen
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.not_now: Not now. Come back when there is something to do.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.attacked: Save it for the training ground.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.arrived: I heard you. This place will do for a camp.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.farewell: Then go with him, and I hope I am wrong about him. If you ever need me, I will hear you.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.farewell_alone: Your own way, then. Walk carefully.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.welcome: Good. We begin here. I will set up camp; come and speak to me when you are ready.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.lesson_one.task: Reach out. Pull five things to you: loose stones, dropped tools, or creatures that mean harm.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.lesson_one.done: You felt how little it takes. Remember that, when you are tempted to take more.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.lesson_two.begin: Blade up. Watch my shoulders, not my saber.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.lesson_two.lost: Enough for now. Breathe, and try again when you are ready.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.lesson_two.done: That is Soresu: the blade as a wall. You will lean on it more than you think.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.spar.interrupted: We stop. A lesson is not worth anyone getting hurt.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.reckoning.brief: There is smoke over the ridge. The poachers have taken settlers. Go, and hold the journal; you will feel the way.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.debrief.captain.yie: She yielded, and you have not decided yet what she is owed.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.debrief.captain.spa: You spared her. That was the harder thing, and the right one.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.debrief.captain.exe: You killed a woman who had already surrendered. I will not pretend that does not trouble me.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.debrief.captain.fle: You let her slip away. She will turn up again somewhere; we will be ready.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.debrief.captain.die: She died in the fighting. That happens. It is still a weight.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.debrief.captives.fr: You cut them loose and asked for nothing. Thank you.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.debrief.captives.ex: You made frightened people pay for their own freedom. That is not what we do.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.debrief.captives.ab: You left them bound. Somebody else had to come for them.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.debrief.ledger: Their ledger. Names, buyers, routes. This is bigger than one crew. I will send it on to the Order.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.debrief.trial: When you are ready, and only then, ask me for the Trial of the Blade.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.trial.lost: Not yet. Rest, and come back to me.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.trial.passed: Kneel. I name you Padawan of the Watch. Let me show you how to mend what is hurt.
npc.oldrepublic.jedi.session.atone: Better. The weight is lighter than it was.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.name: Overseer Teyvar Sorn
npc.oldrepublic.sith.attacked: Save it for the training ground.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.arrived: You called. Here. We make camp.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.farewell: Her, then. You will regret it slowly. The Empire keeps a long memory.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.farewell_alone: Alone. Then die alone, if that is what you want.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.welcome: Good. Camp here. When you are ready to work, speak to me.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.lesson_one.task: Pull three hostile creatures to you and kill each one before it can stand. Quickly.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.lesson_one.done: Better. Now they cannot run from you.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.lesson_two.begin: Brenn. Spar. Do not hold back on my account.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.lesson_two.lost: Pathetic. Again, when you can stand.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.spar.interrupted: Interrupted. Begin again when you can concentrate.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.reckoning.brief: Smoke over the ridge. The scavengers from your cave have a captain now and prisoners. Take back what was stolen. Leave no witnesses.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.debrief.captain.yie: She knelt, and you have not finished her business.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.debrief.captain.spa: You let her go. A witness who knows your face.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.debrief.captain.exe: She begged and you finished it. Good.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.debrief.captain.fle: She ran from you. That will be talked about.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.debrief.captives.fr: You gave them their freedom for nothing. Generous. Foolish.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.debrief.captives.ex: They paid for their lives. That is how the frontier should work.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.debrief.ledger: Their ledger. Buyers in the Core, routes through Imperial space. Useful. I will keep it.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.debrief.trial: When you think you are ready, ask for the Trial of Ascension. Brenn will be waiting.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.trial.begin: Brenn. In earnest, this time. I stop it when one of you cannot continue.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.trial.lost: I stopped it. Next time I might not. Rest.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.trial.passed: Rise, Apprentice. Now I show you what anger is for.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.trial.decide: He yields. His life is yours. Decide.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.trial.killed: Good. He would have done the same.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.session.embrace: Better. You stopped hiding from it.
npc.oldrepublic.sith.session.lost: Again tomorrow, and not like that.
npc.oldrepublic.brenn.name: Brenn Ostrak

item.oldrepublic.poachers_ledger.page1:
Accounts of the crew of H. Dray.

Crystal, raw, cave on the ridge: 3 pcs. Promised to the agent at the Rim market, half paid.

Powder, cells, rations: owed to the quartermaster.
item.oldrepublic.poachers_ledger.page2:
Buyer: 'the collector'. Never comes himself. Pays in Republic credits that smell of the Core.

Asks for colours. Wants the ones that sing.
item.oldrepublic.poachers_ledger.page3:
Second buyer, Imperial. Pays better, asks fewer questions, wants names of anyone who touched the crystals first.

Did not like that one. Took the money.
item.oldrepublic.poachers_ledger.page4:
Note to self: the kid from the cave walked off with the best stone. Find out where they went.

If the homestead pays, we leave the ridge before the snows.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.two_voices.bod:
I dreamt again, but not of the cave. Two voices this time, from far away, one warm as a hearth and one cold as a blade left out overnight. They both knew my name. They both wanted me to come.

When I hold the journal I can feel which way. I think I have to go and see.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_crossing.b:
There were two of them, a woman in sand-coloured robes with a green blade and a man in Imperial grey with a red one, standing a few steps apart with their sabers lit. Neither moved. They were waiting for me.

Whatever I say next will matter for a long time.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_watchwoman:
I chose Master Saelen. She did not smile, exactly, but something in her shoulders let go. The Overseer said something I will not write down and walked away.

She is setting up a camp at the Crossing. Tomorrow, she says, we begin.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_overseer.b:
I chose Overseer Sorn. The Watchwoman looked at me as if I had stepped off a cliff, and maybe I have. Then she was gone.

Sorn has an acolyte, Brenn, who looked at me the way a dog looks at another dog. I think I will be fighting him a lot.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.my_own_way.bod:
I said no to both of them. The Watchwoman nodded as if she had expected it; the Overseer laughed. Then they were gone, and it was only me and the wind on the ridge.

Strange: I feel lighter. Whatever is out there, I will meet it on my own terms.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_reach.body:
Pulling is harder than pushing, and easier at the same time. It is not about strength. It is about wanting the thing to come to me without forcing it.

Master Saelen says that is the whole lesson in one sentence. I think she is only half joking.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.what_is_owed.b:
Drag them in, cut them down. Three times. The third one I barely saw; it was in front of me and then it was not anything at all.

Sorn said 'better'. From him that is a speech.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_still_blad:
She attacked me slowly, the way you would walk a child through a dance, and I still missed the first one. Then I stopped trying to hit back and just turned her blade away. Again. Again.

Soresu. A wall made of light.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.relentless.bod:
Brenn hides behind his guard like a man behind a door. I stopped knocking and kicked it in.

Ataru. No pause, no breath, no mercy in the rhythm. My arms still shake writing this.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.smoke_on_the_r:
There is smoke rising off a ridge in the distance: the cutters from the cave, regrouped under a new captain. They raided a homestead and took people.

I know which way to go.
Hessa Dray knelt in the dirt and asked me not to kill her, and I didn't. She gave me her ledger and walked away without looking back.

I keep thinking she will be someone else's problem now. Maybe mine again, one day.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.a_debt_collect:
She yielded. I killed her anyway.

I am trying to decide whether that was justice or something else. The ledger was in her coat.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.she_ran.title: She Ran
journal.oldrepublic.entry.she_ran.body: I turned away for too long and the captain ran. By the time I looked back there was only her ledger in the dirt by the posts.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.she_fell.title: She Fell
journal.oldrepublic.entry.she_fell.body: The captain died in the fighting, before anyone could decide anything. Her ledger was still on her.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.cut_loose.body:
I cut the ropes and told them to go home. One of them cried. One of them thanked me three times and then ran before I could change my mind.

I would not have.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_price_of_f:
I told them their freedom had a price, and they paid it: everything they had left in their packs. Then I let them go.

The frontier is hard. That is what I told myself.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.left_bound.bod: I left them tied to the posts. Somebody will come for them. Probably.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_ledger.bod:
The captain's ledger: crystals, prices, and two buyers who never give names. One pays in Republic credits, the other in Imperial ones.

Somebody far away is very interested in caves like mine.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_watchwoman:
I told Master Saelen everything. She listened without interrupting, which was worse than if she had.

When I finished she was quiet for a long time, and then she told me what she thought. I am still thinking about it.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_overseer_w:
I reported to Sorn. He asked short questions and wrote nothing down. At the end he looked at me the way a merchant looks at a scale.

I think I came out heavier than he expected. Or lighter.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.the_dark_cloud:
Master Saelen says the dark clouds me, and that she will not test me until it lifts. She was not angry. That made it worse.

She says to meditate beside her, a little each day, and let it go.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.still_too_soft:
Sorn says I am still too soft for the trial. He says it like a diagnosis.

He wants me to kneel beside him each day and stop flinching from what I am.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.padawan_of_the:
I duelled Master Saelen and she stopped, and lowered her blade, and called me Padawan.

Then she put her hand on a cut on my arm and it closed. She says she will teach me that, too.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.apprentice.bod:
I beat Brenn. Sorn named me Apprentice, and then he showed me what the Force does when you stop holding back the anger. Lightning, from my own hands.

I cannot stop looking at them.
journal.oldrepublic.entry.no_master.body:
The ridge is quiet. The crew is broken, the captives are dealt with, and nobody told me what to do about any of it.

No master. No order. Just what I chose. The Force feels close tonight, closer than it ever has.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.jedi_order.tit: The Jedi in the Cold Peace
journal.oldrepublic.codex.jedi_order.bod: Notes gathered: the Jedi Order lost its Temple when Coruscant fell, and signed nothing; the Republic signed for it. Since the treaty the Order keeps to its own work, quietly: teaching, guarding, and watching the borders for the Empire's next move.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.sith_empire.bo: Notes gathered: the Sith Empire came back out of the dark after a thousand years and took Coruscant in a day. The treaty gave it worlds and time. It is ruled by Sith Lords under an Emperor nobody has seen, and every Imperial I have met speaks of strength as if it were a currency.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.jedi_watch.bod: Notes gathered: a Watchman (or Watchwoman) is a Jedi who keeps one sector of space, alone or nearly so, for years. They know every settler and every smuggler. They are the Order's eyes on the frontier, and often the only Jedi anyone here has ever met.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.sith_overseers: Notes gathered: Overseers find Force-sensitive children and adults across the galaxy and send them to the academy on Korriban, where most of them die. Some Overseers are Sith; all of them are measured by how many survive.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.the_frontier.b: Notes gathered: homesteaders, prospectors, a few traders, and nobody in charge. The Republic is far away and the Empire is not welcome. Settlers remember who helped them and who did not, and they talk.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.light_and_dark: Notes gathered: every tradition says the Force has two sides. The Jedi call the light selfless and the dark selfish; the Sith call the light weak and the dark honest. What I do moves me toward one or the other, and the people who teach the Force notice.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.saber_forms.bo: Notes gathered: there are seven classic forms of lightsaber combat. Soresu, Form Three, is a defence so tight nothing gets through. Ataru, Form Four, is speed and acrobatics and never stopping. A duellist keeps one form ready at a time.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.force_heal.bod: Notes gathered: a Jedi can lend the Force to a body to close wounds and steady breath. It costs the healer, a little. Masters of it are rare and loved.
journal.oldrepublic.codex.force_lightnin: Notes gathered: the Sith call it the purest expression of the dark side: hatred made visible, crackling from the fingertips. It burns the target and leaves the caster shaking.
